requirement:
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.

A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test sources only and did not request implementation source. The five tests marked `{test}` for `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` cover each obligation in its text.

**Every function or method with a body is considered.**
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]` builds a source with an `impl` method, a `#[test]` function and a helper inside `mod tests`. It asserts that `impl[S]/fn[method]`, `mod[tests]/fn[case]` and `mod[tests]/fn[helper]` each report "zero execution".
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` asserts that a default trait method body (`#trait[T]/fn[body]`) reports "zero execution".
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent]` covers nested functions and closures. It checks that the outer and inner functions are separate obligations, and that execution of the inner one does not cover the outer.

**Declarations without bodies create no obligations.**
- The default-trait-bodies test asserts that `fn[declaration]` never appears in the report.
- It also asserts that a file holding only a bodiless trait declaration yields `inventory(...).1 == true`. I read that flag as "no executable obligations", an inference from the test's use of it, not something I confirmed in source.
- Macro invocations and derives produce no function obligations (`inventory(...).1` is false for both).
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` asserts that a file with only a struct and a bodiless trait declaration reports "no executable obligations — pass".

**Discovery and parse failures fail the check.**
- The unmeasured-files test writes `fn malformed(` and asserts `!result.passed` and "cannot parse rust source".
- The methods test corrupts `.git/index`. It asserts `!result.passed` and "cannot discover reference sources".

**Functions whose measurement cannot be established are reported as not measured.**
- The default-trait-bodies test asserts that a `#[cfg(any())]` function reports `#fn[excluded]: not measured`. It also asserts that the run fails.
- The unmeasured-files test uses empty function data for a file with a body. It asserts "code.rs: not measured — FAIL" and `#fn[missing]: not measured`.
- Because these cases fail and the tests set up no exception, they check that build-configuration exclusions need exception evidence under `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.

**First-party scope.**
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor]` checks the project-root `vendor` exclusion required by `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`. It asserts that `src/vendor/first_party.rs` is included and fails the check, and that the root `vendor/foreign.rs` is not.

I found no obligation without a test that exercises it and asserts its outcome. The tests I read have no gaps that the cited requirements would expose.

text: :::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
